characters.description: A sixteen-year-old boy who narrates the story from a rest facility in California some months after the events. As the book opens he is finishing his time at Pencey Prep, a Pennsylvania boarding school from which he has just been expelled for failing most of his classes. Cynical, lonely, and preoccupied with what he sees as the phoniness of the adult world, he is also tender toward children and quietly haunted by the loss of his younger brother. He speaks in a candid, digressive, slang-filled voice.
characters.name: Holden Caulfield

characters.description: Holden's older brother, a gifted short-story writer whom Holden admires. D.B. now lives in California and writes for the movies in Hollywood, which Holden regards as a kind of selling out. He served in the army during the war.
characters.name: D.B.

characters.description: A student who rooms next to Holden at Pencey Prep. Older-looking, with a pimply face, bad teeth, and poor hygiene, he is socially awkward and intrusive, wandering uninvited into Holden's room. Holden finds him irritating but is also aware of how friendless and unhappy he is.
characters.name: Robert Ackley

characters.description: Holden's roommate at Pencey Prep, a handsome, athletic, and self-satisfied senior who is popular with girls. Careless about other people's feelings, he asks Holden to write an English composition for him while he goes out on a date. Holden is unsettled to learn the date is with a girl he knows and cares about.
characters.name: Ward Stradlater

characters.description: A girl Holden grew close to over past summers and remembers with warmth and protectiveness. She does not appear in person, but she stays on Holden's mind, especially once he learns she is the date his roommate Stradlater is taking out. He repeatedly thinks of phoning her but never quite manages to.
characters.name: Jane Gallagher

characters.description: Holden's younger brother, who died of leukemia a few years before the events of the story. Holden remembers him as unusually bright, kind, and red-haired. Allie's left-handed baseball glove, covered with poems he had copied onto it, is the subject of the composition Holden writes, and his death is a wound Holden has never recovered from. On the night Allie died, Holden broke the garage windows with his fist.
characters.name: Allie Caulfield

characters.description: Holden's ten-year-old sister, whom he describes with deep affection as clever, pretty, red-haired, and emotionally perceptive far beyond her years. She loves to write stories and to dance. She is the person Holden most wants to see and talk to, and the one he trusts more than anyone.
characters.name: Phoebe Caulfield

characters.description: A pretty, socially confident girl Holden has dated before and telephones to arrange an outing while he is in New York. Poised and conventional, she moves easily in the polished social world that Holden is drawn to and scorns at the same time.
characters.name: Sally Hayes

characters.description: A former English teacher of Holden's, now teaching at a university in New York, whom Holden respects as one of the few adults who seemed to understand him. Holden goes to his apartment late at night seeking a place to stay and some guidance, and Antolini offers him earnest advice about the self-destructive path he seems to be on.
characters.name: Mr. Antolini

recaps.ending: Holden secretly visits his younger sister Phoebe at home, and later at her school and the museum. He shares with her his dream of being the catcher in the rye, the one who saves children from falling off a cliff, revealing how badly he wants to protect innocence. After fleeing his old teacher Mr. Antolini's apartment in alarm, he decides to hitchhike out west and disappear, living as a deaf-mute so he never has to speak to anyone phony again. When he goes to say goodbye to Phoebe, she shows up with a suitcase and demands to come along. Unwilling to drag her into his flight, Holden gives up the plan to calm her, and instead they go to the Central Park zoo and carousel. As he watches Phoebe ride the carousel in the rain, he is flooded with happiness and decides not to run away. The final chapter is narrated from the California facility where he is now being treated. He declines to say what happens next, mentions that he is meant to start a new school in the fall, and admits that telling the story has left him missing almost everyone in it, even the people who treated him badly.
recaps.in_short: Sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield narrates, from a rest home where he is recovering, the story of the few days after he is expelled from Pencey Prep boarding school. Rather than go straight home to face his parents, he leaves early and spends several aimless, lonely days and nights in New York City. He drifts through hotels, bars, and nightclubs; has an unsettling encounter with a prostitute and her pimp; goes on a failed date with Sally Hayes; and grows steadily more depressed by what he sees as the phoniness and cruelty of the adult world, all while grieving his younger brother Allie, who died of leukemia. He finally sneaks home to see his beloved little sister Phoebe and confides his fantasy of being a catcher in the rye who keeps children from harm. After a frightening night at a former teacher's apartment, he resolves to run away, but Phoebe's determination to come with him stops him. Watching her ride a carousel, he chooses to stay, and he later ends up in treatment.

recaps.text: The narrator, sixteen-year-old Holden Caulfield, recounts the days leading up to a breakdown from which he is now recovering in California. He is being expelled from Pencey Prep for failing his classes, and on his last weekend there he visits his old history teacher, puts up with his awkward, intrusive dormmate Ackley, and agrees to write an English composition for his self-assured roommate Stradlater. For the assignment, Holden writes about the poem-covered baseball glove of his younger brother Allie, who died of leukemia. When Stradlater returns from a date with Jane Gallagher, a girl Holden cares deeply about, and dismisses the composition, the two fight and Stradlater bloodies Holden's nose. Fed up and depressed, Holden decides to leave school days before the term officially ends. He packs his things and takes a late train toward New York City, planning to stay in a hotel until his parents have cooled off about the expulsion.

In New York, Holden checks into the shabby Edmont Hotel and spends a restless night failing to connect with anyone. He keeps asking cab drivers where the ducks in Central Park go when the lagoon freezes over. He visits the hotel nightclub and dances with some older tourists, then travels to a Greenwich Village bar full of people he finds phony. Lonely and unable to sleep, he accepts an offer from the elevator operator, Maurice, to send a young prostitute named Sunny up to his room, but when she arrives he only wants to talk and pays her to leave. Later Maurice and Sunny return, demanding more money; Maurice roughs Holden up and takes the cash while Sunny stands by. Throughout the night, Holden's thoughts keep circling back to his little sister Phoebe, to Jane Gallagher, and to his dead brother Allie.

The next day Holden wanders the city. He gives money to two kind nuns he meets at breakfast, buys a record for Phoebe, and is cheered by a small boy he hears singing a song about catching bodies coming through the rye. He takes a date, Sally Hayes, to a play and ice skating, then impulsively urges her to run away with him to live in the woods; when she refuses and he insults her, she leaves in tears. He meets an older former schoolmate, Carl Luce, for drinks, then keeps drinking alone until he is drunk. He goes back to Central Park to look for the ducks, dropping and breaking Phoebe's record on the way, and, cold and miserable, decides to sneak home to see his sister.

Holden sneaks into his family's apartment and wakes Phoebe, who is thrilled until she realizes he has been expelled again. He tells her his one true wish: to be the catcher in the rye, standing at the edge of a cliff to catch children playing in a field of rye before they fall off. When their parents come home he hides, then slips out to stay with a former teacher, Mr. Antolini. Antolini gives him serious advice, but Holden wakes to find the man patting his head in the dark, is frightened, and flees. Exhausted and feeling that he is vanishing, he plans to hitchhike west and live as a deaf-mute, and goes to say goodbye to Phoebe. She arrives with a packed suitcase, insisting on coming with him; to change her mind, he abandons the plan and takes her to the Central Park carousel instead. Watching her ride it in the rain, he feels a sudden, overwhelming happiness. In a brief closing chapter he says only that he later became ill, is now in treatment, and finds himself missing everyone he has described.

characters.description: Acting leader of Twilight Melody while Ryun is away, Anrosh is a cultivator and shield fighter who has reshaped her class around cold and defense. She refuses to accept subordination by the core sect pressing into the frontier and has trained in shield use with Nayra.
characters.name: Anrosh Kesh

characters.description: Anrosh’s bonded awakened sword, which encourages her to pursue strong one-on-one fights.
characters.name: Kagehime

characters.description: A stronger shield fighter who has instructed Anrosh in shield use.
characters.name: Nayra

characters.description: Nayra’s awakened spear.
characters.name: Erishi

characters.description: Nayra's twin sister, whose departure remains part of Nayra's difficult history with her influential family. Reyla stayed with that family after Nayra left, and their separation has left Nayra uncertain about the bond they once shared.
characters.name: Reyla

characters.description: The peak-monarch son of Green Rain's sect leader and its representative in a formal duel with Twilight Melody. His defeat obligates him to serve Twilight Melody under the agreed terms.
characters.name: Green Rain leader's son

characters.description: Leader of a concealed mountain faction, Kael cultivates tranquility to contain the wrath that once overwhelmed his reason. He trades a destructive tournament asset to outside allies while remaining cautious about deeper cooperation.
characters.name: Kael

characters.description: An emissary whose allies have discovered Kael's hidden base. Eric claims they have protected its secrecy, completes an exchange for a dangerous tournament device, and asks Kael to expand their cooperation.
characters.name: Eric

characters.description: The head of Twilight Melody and a void cultivator who has spent roughly a year training alone. Ryun seeks a guiding ideal beyond the pursuit of power, even as he risks his life gathering the essence needed for his next advancement.
characters.name: Ryun Nacht

characters.description: Ryun's contracted wolf partner and a stealth hunter who specializes in isolating powerful prey. After training separately because their fighting styles interfered with each other, Ereclaw reunites with Ryun for a dangerous dungeon expedition.
characters.name: Ereclaw

characters.description: A blind cultivator who instructs Nayra, Anrosh, and Kri in cultivation and advancement. Tali gives practical guidance while expecting her students to make their own defining choices.
characters.name: Tali

characters.description: Anrosh's daughter and a young Twilight Melody trainee. Kri studies footwork and spear fundamentals under Nayra while Tali supervises her cultivation, limits her early skills, and helps prevent premature advancement.
characters.name: Kri

characters.description: Nayra's sister and a captured family operative who was found conducting covert surveillance. Daria warns that Nayra's powerful relatives may eventually authorize her death and believes she may still escape Twilight Melody custody.
characters.name: Daria

characters.description: Ryun's deceased former partner, whose loss continues to shape his grief, loneliness, and isolation. The remaining half of a true-death power they once shared is, to Ryun, evidence that Melody is truly gone.
characters.name: Melody

characters.description: A Twilight Melody warrior killed by a monster. Tio becomes the first dead sect member whom Nayra is shown guiding through the ethereal realm, where she must help him accept his death and continue toward the afterlife.
characters.name: Tio

characters.description: Reyla's older brother and a fire-focused caster on her dungeon team. Emrys helps destroy the monster-filled hazards of Howling Gorge, and their shared training has brought them closer before Reyla returns to the family manor.
characters.name: Emrys

characters.description: An influential older sister of Nayra and Reyla and the leader of a mercenary company. Vanessa joins the family gathering called to address the older siblings' authority over Nayra and the threat created by their decisions.
characters.name: Vanessa

characters.description: Reyla and Nayra’s father. He accepts responsibility for the family’s failures and opposes any plan to kill Nayra.
characters.name: Father Ender

characters.description: A broker capable of granting dangerous bargains. The Dealmaker offers Ryun a way to contain the memories and emotions feeding his mental collapse, but demands an unspecified favor that may be called in far in the future.
characters.name: the Dealmaker

characters.description: A survivor of seventh-iteration Earth and a powerful Warden fighter traveling with Neha. Zach follows a Deep Earth Elemental into its essence plane to destroy it, then gains the opportunity to form a permanent True Link.
characters.name: Zacharia Gardner

characters.description: Zach's shapeshifting Warden partner, whose several bodies are all expressions of the same person. She fights beside Zach, forms a voluntary True Link with him, and chooses to remove her cultivation in hopes of correcting a dangerous imbalance.
characters.name: Neha

characters.description: The Warden leader who offers Zach a vacant place on the organization's tournament team while assigning more experienced Wardens to city security.
characters.name: Warden commander

characters.description: An unnamed cultivator encountered by Ryun at a Dal Dvor inn. She is traveling to the tournament after unsuccessful business in the Under and displays cultivation beyond the realms familiar to him.
characters.name: tattooed cultivator

characters.description: A minotaur hammer fighter who leads Zach's Warden tournament team.
characters.name: Oakham

characters.description: A sociable member of the masquerade's host sect and an ambitious High Division contender. Riki introduces himself to Ryun's delegation after passing the first tournament qualifier, approaching the visiting sect with easy confidence.
characters.name: Riki

characters.description: Ierv's son and a High Division competitor who confronts Ryun over the deaths of his aunt and cousin and the defeat of his father. Iari apologizes after insulting Ierv, though his feelings about the conflict remain unresolved.
characters.name: Iari

characters.description: A powerful leader of the hosting great sect, also known as the Spear of Sorrow. Celia offers to sponsor Ryun personally and seeks a formal connection with Twilight Melody, though she has not yet explained all of her motives.
characters.name: Celia

characters.description: A powerful drake who opens the High Division free-for-all. Zenker presents the contestants as possible future high-rankers at the start of a qualifier where serious injury remains a genuine danger.
characters.name: Zenker

characters.description: A young Minotaur with exceptional spatial abilities whom Kael rescued from slavery. Formerly bound by contract to an immortal, he is Kael's strongest but reluctant ally and is essential to a plan Kael has not disclosed.
characters.name: young Minotaur spatial savant

characters.description: Kael's senior adviser, who counsels him against becoming more deeply involved with Eric's group.
characters.name: Gior

characters.description: A High Division tournament fighter specializing in rifles. His enhanced guns and ammunition make his long-range attacks exceptionally powerful but expensive to use.
characters.name: Gior

characters.description: An awakened blacksmithing forge found among the top-eight tournament rewards. Brightstar chooses Ryun as its bearer, asks to be fed interesting objects, and can store, repair, reproduce, or gradually improve suitable equipment.
characters.name: Brightstar

recaps.ending: Ryun's High Division run ends in the top eight when Riki uses a newly gained Ideal to defeat him. Ryun bonds the awakened forge Brightstar as his reward, but the tournament is then overtaken by a portal breach. An apparently endless monster force pours into the arena while more monsters move through Tournament City to surround the defenders. Ryun sends Ereclaw to help Anrosh evacuate Twilight Melody and joins Celia in holding the wall. He gives Celia the complementary half of the true-death power once shared with Melody, linking Ryun and Celia mentally and emotionally until one of them dies. Zach and Neha remain with the Warden response. The commander considers Zach essential to closing the portal and prepares to protect him during the attempt, while another group secures the healing building as a possible evacuation route. The portal is still open, the defenders are nearly encircled, and the empire's advancing swarm and Kael's separate operation remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Twilight Melody resists Green Rain, then travels to the Centennial Tournament despite Nayra's warning that her hidden homeland is planning war and an operation at the event. Nayra breaks the class bond controlling her growth, while Anrosh becomes an immortal protector through Ryun's inspiration. Ryun finds an Ideal centered on witnessing chosen final ends. Zach arrives with Neha, learns that the Wardens know her concealed identity, and confronts Ryun over the massacre that killed his family, but chooses present duty over immediate revenge. Nayra reaches the top 32 of her solo division. Ryun reaches the High Division top eight before Riki defeats him, then bonds the awakened forge Brightstar. A monster army breaches the arena portal, forcing Ryun and Celia to defend the wall while Twilight Melody evacuates. Ryun gives Celia the other half of the true-death power, permanently linking them. Zach is selected for the attempt to close the still-open portal as the city approaches encirclement.

recaps.text: Previously: Ryun Nacht, a survivor of seventh-iteration Earth, became the head of Twilight Melody in the Infinite Realm. His rise followed violence that left Zacharia Gardner searching for him. Ryun also lost his partner Melody, and the aftermath of her death remains bound to a dangerous true-death power and to a bargain with the Dealmaker. Anrosh Kesh has taken responsibility for Twilight Melody during Ryun's absences, with Nayra serving as one of the sect's strongest fighters and trusted leaders within Twilight Melody. Nayra has separated herself from an influential family and from her twin, Reyla. Zach has meanwhile joined the Wardens and travels with Neha, a shapeshifter whose many bodies belong to one person. Their partnership has become central to both of them, even as Neha's unusual combination of powers threatens her stability. Ryun and Zach are now moving through the same wider world, with their unfinished history still between them.

So far this book: Anrosh advances and returns to find Green Rain pressing Twilight Melody to accept subordinate status. She refuses, rescues captured sect members through a force led by Nayra, and turns the dispute into a formal representative duel. Nayra defeats Green Rain's heir, ending the immediate demand and binding him to service in Twilight Melody. Elsewhere, Kael trades a destructive tournament device to Eric's allies while resisting a larger commitment to their cause. Ryun completes a year of solitary training at the edge of the void. He survives exposure to its ninth tier, gains the essence he needs, and advances to early immortality on the Path of the Final End. He rejects a rebirth that might let him evade his past and instead takes a void-based immortal form. Although his body and power have changed, he still lacks the guiding Ideal he has been seeking. With his advancement complete, he turns back toward Twilight Melody.

Ryun reunites with Ereclaw, tests his new abilities in a dangerous dungeon, and returns to Twilight Melody. Nayra advances, begins a relationship with Anrosh, and helps train Anrosh's daughter Kri under Tali's guidance. The sect receives an invitation to the Centennial Tournament, and Ryun orders the leadership to accept and organize a trading caravan. Before departure, he detects a covert operation centered on Nayra. The captured watcher is Daria, one of Nayra's sisters, who warns that their family may ultimately sanction Nayra's death. Nayra then discloses the larger danger: she comes from a hidden empire founded by exiled third-iteration rankers. That empire is preparing for war against the Core and has an undisclosed plan involving the tournament. Ryun still decides to attend. He keeps Daria in service to repay the intrusion, releases her companions with a warning, and treats any further move against Nayra as a threat to Twilight Melody.

Nayra guides the dead warrior Tio through the ethereal realm, helps him accept his death, and returns with a new boon. She then advances to level 300 and chooses the unique Heart of Gunner class, breaking Reyla's ability to dictate their shared class evolution while preserving their Twin Link. The resulting contact brings Nayra's family conflict into the open. Reyla erases her own cultivation to make room for a different path, while their parents confront the older siblings who considered killing Nayra. They forbid any further attempt on her life. A look into Ryun's past shows why his grief became so dangerous after Melody died: a remnant tied to their divided true-death power fed on his rage and loss. The Dealmaker contained it by sealing the memories and emotions that sustained it, in return for a future favor. Zach and Neha, meanwhile, defeat a Deep Earth Elemental. Zach forms a True Link with Neha, and she removes her cultivation in an attempt to correct her unstable condition. She survives the treatment, and they begin their journey back toward the Wardens and the tournament.

Zach and Neha reach Tournament Territory, where Zach accepts a place on a Warden team. Twilight Melody travels through Dal Dvor while Ryun struggles with grief, loneliness, and his unfinished Ideal. A brief encounter with a powerful traveling cultivator helps him accept that moving forward does not betray Melody, and he begins to understand endings as a source of meaning. At Tournament City, Twilight Melody establishes a compound, registers Nayra for the mid division and Ryun for the High Division, and converts valuable materials into resources for the sect. Ryun's origin as a survivor of seventh-iteration Earth becomes public during registration. Ereclaw is barred from competing as Ryun's partner, while Daria is assigned to protect the compound under her one-year service obligation. Anrosh also asks Ereclaw whether he killed her husband before joining Ryun, but he cannot give a certain answer. Zach trains in private, raises his level, and prepares to serve as the Warden team's concealed advantage in its first qualifier.

Zach helps the Warden team survive its first qualifier and advances to level 359, but further class growth requires an immortal evolution. Watching the Wardens fight convinces Anrosh that Twilight Melody needs a permanent defender. Ryun shares his inspiration with her, allowing her to advance to immortality at the cost of tying her future cultivation development to his. Ryun then wins his own opening qualifier through long-range void shaping and evolves his perception, though the match exposes his limited core capacity. Contact from a great sect draws Ryun and Anrosh to a masquerade, where they meet the High Division contender Riki. Celia, the Spear of Sorrow, offers Ryun personal sponsorship and seeks a closer relationship with Twilight Melody. During the gathering, Ryun encounters an elderly ranker who has chosen true death. He listens to her life and fulfills her request for a final end. The experience completes his Ideal: he will witness, understand, and remember lives at their chosen endings. He gains the power of The Witness of Journey's End, while Celia's offer remains undecided.

Ryun survives the High Division free-for-all and joins its final 32. Zach recognizes him during the broadcast as the man responsible for the massacre that killed Zach's wife and child. Zach confronts him but does not attack. Neha argues that revenge would endanger them, expose her, and threaten the tournament peace, and Zach chooses their shared future and the protection of others over immediate vengeance. The Warden commander then reveals that the Wardens already knew Neha's concealed identity and past. She orders Neha's current Warden identity retired but allows the pair to continue under supervision. While Neha changes bodies, Zach adopts protection rather than revenge as his guiding purpose. He seeks an immortal-class quest from the Dealmaker and chooses the relic-rarity Lord of the Aspects, a demanding solo path involving powerful elementals, dragons, aspect planes, and mastery in combat. The Dealmaker confirms that outside influence did not absolve Ryun of his crimes, and Zach accepts that Ryun alone bears responsibility for them.

Neha returns in a new body, while Zach's Warden team is eliminated after an elite sect isolates him from his allies. Nayra unveils her Scorching Mist path in the solo tournament and wins a difficult match, but an adaptive drake shifter counters her fire and cloud form in the next round. She leaves the competition in the top 32, and all Twilight Melody entrants have improved the sect's reputation despite their defeats. Ryun continues meeting Celia and considers her sponsorship without accepting her undisclosed agenda. Beyond the matches, the threat around the tournament sharpens. Kael breaks with Eric and plans to exploit the disruption expected from the empire's reaction engine for a separate purpose involving a rescued Minotaur spatial savant. Far away, Reyla watches the empire's great swarm absorb another sovereign monster and its forces. The growing invasion is moving toward the Core while imperial armies follow behind it.

Before his opening main-bracket match, Ryun upgrades his second cultivation path and uses an elixir to reform his core for greater capacity. He defeats the rifle specialist Gior by enduring devastating long-range fire and using his new Ideal power to break the attack's momentum. His next match against Riki becomes a contest of repeated bodily destruction and reconstruction. Riki ultimately wins with a newly acquired Ideal after Ryun declines to use his own most decisive ability. Ryun still earns a top-eight reward and bonds an awakened forge named Brightstar, which can store, repair, reproduce, and improve equipment. The tournament then collapses into crisis when an apparently endless monster force pours through the arena portal. Monsters already in Tournament City move to encircle the defenders. Ryun sends Ereclaw to help Anrosh evacuate Twilight Melody and joins Celia on the arena wall. He gives Celia the complementary half of the true-death power once shared with Melody, granting them a joint slowing power and binding their minds and emotions until one dies. Zach and Neha remain with the Wardens. The commander prepares to protect Zach during an attempt to close the portal, while a separate force secures the healing building for evacuation. A distant assault briefly clears part of the horde, but the portal remains open and the defenders are still close to encirclement.

characters.description: A young man in Baltimore's criminal underworld, very large, very strong, and unnervingly calm. He works as muscle and a driver for a small crew, is well liked by people who do not need him to explain himself, and does not react to violence the way those around him expect. He has no family except the woman who took him in as a child, and no ambition beyond the day in front of him.
characters.name: Timmy

characters.description: The leader of the small crew Timmy works for, a clever young thief and hacker with a withered arm and an aggressive intelligence. He runs jobs on the edges of the city's larger organizations and is smart enough to know exactly how small he still is.
characters.name: Erich

characters.description: An aging woman who has spent her life at the bottom of the city's economy and who took Timmy in when he was a child, protecting him and giving him the only stable attachment he has. She has a long history with the men who run Baltimore's underworld, and she knows more about their business than is safe for her.
characters.name: Lydia Maalouf

characters.description: The man who runs organized crime in this part of Baltimore, established, careful, and entirely unsentimental about the people who work for him. He has survived previous crackdowns by being willing to shed anything that might connect him to a charge.
characters.name: Burton

recaps.ending: The crackdown forces Burton to clean house, and Lydia is one of the loose ends he decides to remove. Timmy kills him for it. That solves Lydia's problem and creates a much larger one: the killing cannot be hidden, and staying on Earth means dying for it. Erich, who has the skills and now the motive, forges Timmy an identity out of the dead man's name and papers, and Timmy leaves Baltimore and Earth entirely, shipping out for the Belt as Amos Burton. Lydia stays behind, alive, safe, and out of his life for good; the parting is the price of the rescue. Erich inherits what is left of the organization and becomes the man who runs that corner of the city. The story ends with Timmy in transit, remade into someone with a stolen name, no history anyone can check, and no intention of ever coming back down a gravity well.
recaps.in_short: In a Baltimore where the legal economy has largely stopped needing people, a young enforcer called Timmy works for Erich, a sharp, physically disabled crew boss operating at the edges of the local crime organization run by a man named Burton. Periodically the authorities flood the city and break the underworld apart, a cycle everyone calls the churn, and one has just begun. As Burton starts eliminating anyone who could implicate him, the danger reaches Lydia Maalouf, the aging woman who raised Timmy and is the only person he is genuinely attached to. Timmy kills Burton to protect her, which saves her life and ends his own life in the city. Erich forges him a new identity from the dead man's name, and Timmy leaves Earth for the Belt as Amos Burton, while Erich takes over the organization. Lydia survives, and Timmy never sees her again.

recaps.text: This novella is a prequel and stands alone. It is set on Earth, in Baltimore, years before the events of the first novel, and requires no knowledge of the series: no ships, no alien technology, and no politics beyond one city's. Its background is the Earth the novels describe from a distance. Most of the population lives on basic support with no work available to them, the legal economy has no use for them, and what remains is an informal one run by criminal organizations that periodically get flattened by a police surge and then reassemble. That cycle is called the churn. The story follows a young enforcer in one of the small crews caught in the middle of one.

Timmy works as muscle and driver for Erich, who runs a small crew on the fringes of Burton's organization in Baltimore. It is a functional arrangement: Erich thinks, Timmy does what is needed, and neither of them is important enough to attract attention. Timmy's one real tie is to Lydia Maalouf, the woman who took him in as a child and who has spent her life close to the men who run the city's underworld. Then the churn begins. A large security force floods the district, arrests sweep through the organizations from the bottom up, and everyone who has been operating comfortably has to decide what they can afford to be caught holding. Burton, who has survived these cycles before, begins cutting away anything that could connect him to a charge, and the people who know his history become liabilities rather than assets.

Lydia is on Burton's list. Timmy kills him for it, which protects her and makes it impossible for Timmy to remain in the city or on the planet. Erich, who benefits from the vacancy and is genuinely attached to Timmy in his own way, forges him an identity from the dead man's name and papers. Timmy leaves Baltimore and Earth, shipping out to the Belt as Amos Burton, with no history that will survive a background check and no plan to return. Lydia stays behind, alive and out of danger, and the separation is permanent. Erich takes over what is left of the organization and becomes the man who runs that part of Baltimore.

characters.description: A young woman scraping a living in Ottoman Cairo as a thief, a fake exorcist and a healer for hire. She has no memory of her parents, speaks an unusual number of languages including one she has never been able to place, and hides a talent she cannot explain: she senses sickness in others by touch, and her own injuries close almost as fast as she takes them. Sharp-tongued, mercenary and relentlessly practical, she treats every relationship as a transaction, until a ceremony she is performing purely for money summons something she cannot talk her way out of.
characters.name: Nahri

characters.description: A daeva warrior who appears out of the desert air when Nahri sings in a language she does not know she speaks. Tall and green-eyed, marked with a faded tattoo of ladder-like rungs and wearing a battered emerald ring, he commands fire and wind and can fly. He served the Nahids, the family of magical healers who ruled the djinn city of Daevabad before it was taken from them, and fourteen centuries of that history sit heavily on him. Arrogant, blunt and quick to violence, he is bound by duty to protect Nahri, whom he believes to be the last of his masters' line. Long stretches of his own past are missing from his memory.
characters.name: Dara

characters.description: An elderly apothecary in Cairo who lets Nahri work beside him, buys the odd item she has stolen, and worries constantly about the risks she takes. He is one of the few people in her life she is genuinely fond of.
characters.name: Yaqub

characters.description: A young girl in Cairo whose family pays Nahri to perform a zar, a ceremony meant to appease the spirit they believe is troubling her. Nahri expects to sing, take the money and leave. The ceremony does not go as she intends.
characters.name: Baseema

characters.description: The younger son of the king of Daevabad, raised from childhood at the Citadel to become Qaid, commander of the army, and to serve his elder brother when that brother takes the throne. Devout, disciplined and awkward anywhere outside a training yard, he is troubled by the way the city treats its shafit, the people of mixed human and djinn blood, and has begun quietly diverting money to an organization that helps them, a betrayal of his father he tells himself is only charity.
characters.name: Alizayd

characters.description: The leader of the Tanzeem, a shafit welfare organization in Daevabad that runs an orphanage, a school and a clinic, and that Ali has been secretly funding. A preacher of mixed human and djinn blood, he argues that the city's laws leave the shafit no lawful way to protect themselves.
characters.name: Anas

characters.description: King of Daevabad and head of the Qahtani family, which took the city from the Nahids fourteen centuries ago. He rules its six djinn tribes from the palace of the brass city and holds Suleiman's seal, the relic whose bearer commands magic within Daevabad's walls. Politically shrewd and entirely unsentimental, he keeps peace between tribes that despise one another by making public examples of anyone who disturbs it.
characters.name: Ghassan

characters.description: Ghassan's elder son and the emir, heir to Daevabad. Charming, worldly and fond of wine, poetry and company, he moves easily among the city's nobles in a way his younger brother never has. He is inseparable from Jamshid e-Pramukh, son of the Daeva grand wazir, and he treats the responsibilities waiting for him with a lightness his family reads as carelessness.
characters.name: Muntadhir

characters.description: Ghassan's daughter and Ali's older sister, a princess raised at court rather than at the Citadel. Poised and very well informed, she reads the palace's politics better than either of her brothers and is often the only easy point of contact between them.
characters.name: Zaynab

characters.description: A peri, one of the beings of the air, who finds Nahri and Dara close to death on their journey east and tends to them. The peri are forbidden to involve themselves in the affairs of daevas and humans, and the help he gives is offered at real risk to himself.
characters.name: Khayzur

characters.description: An officer of Daevabad's Royal Guard who is connected to the Tanzeem and who presses Ali to carry his sympathy for the shafit further than quiet donations. Devout and uncompromising, he has little patience for a prince's scruples.
characters.name: Rashid

characters.description: A Daeva woman who served the last Nahid healers before they died and who now assists Nahri in the palace infirmary, teaching her a craft she was never trained in. Devoted to Daeva tradition and to the restoration of her tribe's standing, she is impatient with Nahri's ignorance and with her friendliness toward the Qahtanis.
characters.name: Nisreen

characters.description: Grand wazir of Daevabad and the highest-ranking Daeva in the king's government, brought to the capital from the tribe's provincial seat. Fiercely protective of Daeva interests and openly hostile to any concession to the shafit, he is in near-constant conflict with Ali.
characters.name: Kaveh

characters.description: The Banu Nahida of the previous generation, remembered as the most gifted healer her family produced and as a woman the king could never quite control. She and her brother Rustam were reported killed by ifrit some twenty years before Nahri arrives, and their deaths left Daevabad with no Nahid healer at all. Everything Nahri hears about her comes secondhand, from people with reasons of their own for how they tell it.
characters.name: Manizheh

characters.description: Kaveh's son, a Daeva archer who serves as Muntadhir's captain and closest companion. Even-tempered and steady, he is one of the very few people at court whom both the Daeva tribe and the Qahtanis are willing to trust.
characters.name: Jamshid

recaps.ending: Nahri agrees to leave Daevabad with Dara, and the escape becomes a massacre: Dara cuts through the soldiers sent to stop them, and Jamshid e-Pramukh is left crippled by his arrows. The chase ends on the cursed lake, where Alizayd is dragged into the water. The marid, the water spirits who cursed the lake long ago, take hold of him and use his body, and the possessed Ali kills Dara. Nahri is brought back to the palace with nothing left to bargain with. She heals Ali of what the marid did to him, and Ghassan buries the truth about the possession, then marries her to his heir Muntadhir immediately, binding the Nahid line to the Qahtanis. Ali is sent away to the Geziri provinces in disgrace, an assignment his family does not expect him to survive. Nahri ends the book a queen in name, isolated, grieving, and with no illusions left about the man who brought her east. The epilogue overturns all of it. Far from the city, Dara wakes: pulled out of a quiet afterlife into a body that is whole, freed of the ifrit's slave curse, and restored to the unbound magic his people held before Suleiman's punishment. Two people are standing over him. One is Kaveh e-Pramukh, Daevabad's grand wazir. The other is Banu Manizheh, the Nahid healer everyone believes the ifrit murdered two decades ago. She is alive, she has been preparing for a generation, and she tells Dara that Nahri is her daughter.
recaps.in_short: Nahri is a young con artist and thief in Ottoman Cairo with a healing gift she cannot explain. Performing a ceremony for money, she accidentally summons Darayavahoush, a daeva warrior who tells her she carries the blood of the Nahids, a family of magical healers, and that her only safe place is Daevabad, a hidden djinn city. Hunted by ifrit, the two cross half the world to reach it. There Nahri is received by the Daeva tribe as their Banu Nahida and installed in the palace of King Ghassan al Qahtani, whose ancestors took the city from hers. She befriends the king's younger son, Ali, a devout prince secretly funding the city's despised part-human shafit, and learns that Dara is remembered by the other tribes as the Scourge of Qui-zi, the author of a massacre. To buy protection, Nahri bargains a betrothal to Ghassan's heir, Muntadhir. When Dara tries to take her out of the city, the escape ends in bloodshed on the cursed lake: the marid seize Ali and use him to kill Dara. Nahri is married to Muntadhir and Ali is exiled. In the epilogue Dara wakes restored to life by Banu Manizheh, the Nahid healer believed dead for twenty years, who reveals that Nahri is her daughter.

recaps.text: Nahri makes a living in Ottoman Cairo as a thief and an unlicensed healer, telling fortunes and staging ceremonies she is certain are pure theatre. She hides a genuine gift: she senses illness by touch, and her own wounds close in moments. During a zar she is paid to hold for a girl named Baseema, she sings in a language she cannot identify, and two things answer. One is an ifrit, an ancient and malevolent being that takes hold of the girl. The other is Darayavahoush, a daeva warrior who arrives in a sandstorm, destroys the creatures hunting her and tells her that her blood is not human. He names her a descendant of the Nahids, a family of magical healers, and says the only place she will be safe is Daevabad, a hidden city far to the east. With ifrit behind them and the dead rising from the ground to follow, the two flee Egypt together.

Traveling east by conjured carpet, by boat and on foot, Dara teaches Nahri what she is. Long ago the prophet Suleiman punished the daevas for meddling with humanity, stripped their magic and returned it altered, splitting them into six tribes: the Daevas, who kept the old name, and the Geziri, Ayaanle, Sahrayn, Agnivanshi and Tukharistani. Those who refused to submit became the ifrit, unchanged and cursed, and they take their revenge by enslaving djinn into rings and by hunting the Nahids, the healer family entrusted with Suleiman's seal. Daevabad itself was taken from the Nahids fourteen centuries ago by Zaydi al Qahtani, and his descendants rule it still. Children of mixed human and djinn blood, the shafit, are confined and despised there. Dara served the Nahids as their Afshin, their warrior, and he speaks of the Qahtanis with open hatred. In Daevabad, meanwhile, Prince Alizayd, the king's younger son, trains to command his brother's army while secretly funding a shafit organization his father would call treason.

The journey grows steadily more dangerous. Ifrit ambush them, ghouls follow their trail, and after one attack a peri named Khayzur finds the pair near death and heals them, breaking his own people's rule against interfering. Nahri presses Dara about the gaps in his history and learns that he spent centuries as an ifrit's slave, passed from one human master to the next, with almost no memory of any of it, before he was freed into a world that had moved on without him. In Daevabad, Ali's payments to the Tanzeem are traced. Its leader, Sheikh Anas, is arrested and publicly executed, taking the blame alone and leaving Ali alive, shaken, and further into the shafit cause than before. Nahri and Dara reach the Gozan river, pass through the veil that hides the road, and come within sight of a city of brass on an island in a cursed lake.

Nahri enters Daevabad as the first Nahid healer in twenty years and is received by her own tribe as their Banu Nahida. King Ghassan installs her in the palace, sets her to work in the infirmary under Nisreen, a Daeva woman who served the previous Nahids, and assigns Ali to tutor her. The two become unlikely friends. Dara's return is far less welcome: to the Geziri he is a war criminal, and he is kept under guard and watched. Nahri finds the city's politics as ruthless as any Cairo street. The Daeva tribe, led by grand wazir Kaveh, wants her as their symbol; the Qahtanis want her contained; the shafit, whose conditions appall her, want a healer willing to treat them; and Nahri's rounded ears mark her as carrying human blood, which almost everyone has an opinion about.

Nahri learns what Dara kept from her. During the war that ended Nahid rule he carried out a massacre at Qui-zi, killing and enslaving its shafit population, and the other tribes remember him as the Scourge. He does not deny it, and his presence makes both of them targets. To buy protection for herself, for the Daeva tribe and for Dara, Nahri negotiates a betrothal to the emir Muntadhir, treating her own marriage as a contract to be haggled over. Ali, drawn back into shafit politics by a Royal Guard officer named Rashid, discovers that the money he handed over bought weapons as well as bread. The fallout costs lives, destroys what remains of his father's trust in him, and leaves him with no clean way out of anything.

The city's tensions come apart. Violence between Daeva and shafit escalates, and Ali, stripped of his standing, is caught between the brother he loves and the cause he cannot abandon. Dara, unwilling to leave Nahri in Qahtani hands and unwilling to accept her marriage, presses her to run with him and raise the Daeva against the king. Nahri, who has spent the whole book refusing to be anyone's property or anyone's banner, has to choose between a bargain she made with her eyes open and the man who brought her here, knowing that whichever she picks, people she has treated will pay for it.

Nahri agrees to go with Dara, and the escape turns into a slaughter. Dara cuts through the guards sent to stop them, and Jamshid is gravely wounded by his arrows. The chase ends on the cursed lake, where Ali is pulled into the water. The marid, the water spirits who cursed the lake long ago, take hold of him and use his body: Ali rises marid-possessed and kills Dara. Nahri is returned to the palace, and Dara's ring is taken from the water. Ali is left dying of what the marid did to him, and Nahri heals him, though Ghassan buries the truth about what took him. The king then makes his terms plain, and Nahri is married to Muntadhir at once. Ali is sent away to the Geziri provinces in disgrace, an assignment few expect him to survive.

In the epilogue, Dara wakes. He is pulled out of a quiet afterlife and back into a whole body, freed of the ifrit's slave curse and restored to the full, unbound magic his people held before Suleiman's punishment. He is not alone. Standing over him are Kaveh e-Pramukh, Daevabad's grand wazir, who has spent the entire book at the king's side, and Banu Manizheh, the Nahid healer the world believes the ifrit murdered twenty years ago. She is alive. She has been preparing for a very long time. And she tells Dara that Nahri is her daughter.

characters.description: A failed student of Unseen University, the Disc's college of wizardry, who was expelled after a single forbidden spell from the Octavo, the world's most powerful grimoire, lodged itself in his mind and crowded out every other. He can cast almost nothing and is a coward by conviction, treating flight as the only sane response to danger and mere survival as an accomplishment. He speaks a number of languages, which makes him useful as a guide. When the Patrician of Ankh-Morpork orders him to protect a visiting foreigner, his quiet, precarious life comes to an end.
characters.name: Rincewind

characters.description: A small, eager man from the wealthy Agatean Empire on the far side of the Disc, and the first tourist the Discworld has ever seen. An insurance clerk by trade, he travels for pleasure with a purse full of gold, an unshakeable belief that almost everyone he meets is good at heart, and a delight in danger he does not recognize as dangerous. He hires Rincewind as guide and interpreter and introduces Ankh-Morpork to the ruinous new idea of insurance.
characters.name: Twoflower

characters.description: A large travelling chest made of sapient pearwood, belonging to Twoflower. It walks on hundreds of little legs, follows its owner with doglike devotion, and holds far more than its size should allow, producing clean laundry from unknown depths. It is utterly loyal and utterly murderous toward anything that threatens its owner, swallowing enemies whole, and it cannot be stopped, reasoned with, or outrun.
characters.name: The Luggage

characters.description: The ruler of Ankh-Morpork, the Disc's greatest and most disreputable city. Shrewd and calculating, he grasps at once that a rich foreign visitor is both an opportunity and a diplomatic hazard, and he charges Rincewind with keeping the tourist alive and content, on pain of death.
characters.name: The Patrician

characters.description: The anthropomorphic personification of death, a robed skeleton who arrives in person to collect the souls of the notable and the interesting and speaks in a voice that lands directly in the mind. He takes a particular, repeatedly thwarted interest in Rincewind, turning up expecting to claim him only to be cheated each time by the wizard's improbable luck.
characters.name: Death

characters.description: One of the Disc's greatest heroes, a heavily muscled warrior who roams in search of treasure, monsters, and fame. Practical about his trade, he briefly takes Rincewind and Twoflower under his protection, drawn chiefly by Twoflower's picture-making box and the promise of reward.
characters.name: Hrun the Barbarian

characters.description: An ancient, malignant entity known as the Sender of Eight, a tentacled evil older than the gods that dwells beneath a lightless temple. Its power is bound up with the number eight, which wizards of the Disc avoid speaking aloud for fear of drawing its attention.
characters.name: Bel-Shamharoth

characters.description: A dragonrider and would-be ruler of the Wyrmberg, an inverted mountain whose people summon dragons out of imagination. Ambitious and commanding, she means to seize the Wyrmberg from her brothers and needs a champion to help her do it.
characters.name: Liessa Wyrmbidder

characters.description: The vast star turtle that swims through space carrying the four world-bearing elephants on its shell, with the Discworld resting upon them. Its age, its sex, and its destination are all unknown, and the question of where it is going underlies the whole of the Disc's cosmology.
characters.name: Great A'Tuin

recaps.ending: The Colour of Magic ends on a literal cliffhanger. Having escaped the scholars of Krull at the Rim of the world, Rincewind and Twoflower are swept over the edge of the Disc and fall, together with the Luggage, off the Rimfall waterfall and out into the void beyond the world. Nothing about their fate is resolved: they simply go over the edge and keep falling, with no rescue and no landing. The two remain bound together, the reluctant wizard and the relentlessly optimistic tourist, still pursued by the bad luck that has followed them the whole way. The larger questions of the setting are left open as well, chief among them the riddle the scholars of Krull hoped to answer, namely where the Great A'Tuin, the star turtle carrying the Disc, is swimming to and why. The story continues directly in the next book.
recaps.in_short: Rincewind, an incompetent and cowardly wizard of Ankh-Morpork, is ordered to protect Twoflower, the Discworld's first tourist, a naive and wealthy insurance clerk from the far Agatean Empire who travels with a fortune in gold and a homicidal walking chest called the Luggage. Their misadventures begin when Twoflower's talk of insurance burns Ankh-Morpork to the ground, and they flee the city with Death and other dangers close behind. They pass through a temple of the ancient evil Bel-Shamharoth, the Sender of Eight; visit the Wyrmberg, an inverted mountain of imaginary dragons ruled by the dragonrider Liessa; and are finally carried to the very Rim of the flat world, where the kingdom of Krull means to launch a ship over the edge and sacrifice them. Escaping, the two are instead swept over the Rimfall. The book ends with Rincewind and Twoflower plunging off the edge of the Disc into open space, their story left hanging.

recaps.text: In Ankh-Morpork the failed wizard Rincewind meets Twoflower, the Disc's first tourist, a cheerful insurance clerk from the distant Agatean Empire who has come to see the world and carries a fortune in gold and a walking chest, the Luggage. The Patrician orders Rincewind to guard the visitor and keep him alive. Twoflower's foreign notion of insurance quickly catches on, and when a tavern owner sets fire to his own premises to collect on it, the blaze spreads and consumes much of the city. Rincewind, who had meant to rob Twoflower and slip away, instead ends up fleeing the burning city at his side, pursued by trouble and by Death himself, who keeps arriving to collect the wizard only to be foiled.

Away from the city, Rincewind and Twoflower travel into wild country, unaware that their fates are literally being gambled over by the gods at a gaming table. They fall in with Hrun the Barbarian, a famous hero, and are drawn to a dark temple dedicated to Bel-Shamharoth, the Sender of Eight, an ancient evil tied to the forbidden number. Trapped inside, they barely survive an encounter with the creature and escape the temple.

The companions come to the Wyrmberg, an upside-down mountain ruled by dragonriders who conjure dragons out of their own imaginations. Twoflower, whose mind is vivid enough to summon a dragon of his own, is caught up in a struggle for control of the mountain between Liessa Wyrmbidder and her brothers, and Hrun becomes entangled in Liessa's schemes. Rincewind and Twoflower escape when their imagined dragons carry them off the mountain, and they fall clear of the Wyrmberg toward the Rim of the world.

The pair are carried to the very edge of the Disc, where the endless waterfall of the Rimfall pours off into space. They reach Krull, a kingdom perched at the Rim whose scholars intend to launch a great bronze vessel over the edge to learn the sex of the Great A'Tuin, and who plan to sacrifice the two travellers to the project. Rincewind and Twoflower escape, but in doing so are swept over the Rim. The book ends with them going over the edge of the world and falling into the void, their fate unresolved.

characters.description: Heir to Illéa and, with her mother gravely ill and her father unwilling to leave her side, acting regent. She is running a country in unrest, a Selection she can no longer treat as theater, and a family missing a brother, all at once. The cold self-sufficiency she began with has been worn down: she now knows she needs people, which she finds harder to manage than governing.
characters.name: Eadlyn Schreave

characters.description: Queen of Illéa, recovering from a heart attack brought on by her son's elopement. She came to the palace as a Five in her husband's Selection and has spent her reign softening the monarchy; she is now too weak to do much of anything, and the household is arranged around her.
characters.name: America Schreave

characters.description: King of Illéa, who abolished the caste system twenty years ago and has spent his reign managing the consequences. With his wife's life in danger he hands the day-to-day rule of the country to his daughter and refuses to be moved from America's side.
characters.name: Maxon Schreave

characters.description: Eadlyn's twin brother, now living in France with Princess Camille after eloping without warning. His absence is a wound in the family and a political problem, and he and Eadlyn are still repairing what he did.
characters.name: Ahren Schreave

characters.description: Eadlyn's younger brother, thoughtful and steady, and more use to her in a crisis than she had ever assumed a younger sibling could be.
characters.name: Kaden Schreave

characters.description: One of the six remaining Selected, raised inside the palace and a fixture in Eadlyn's life since childhood. He wants to design buildings rather than hold a title, and he is honest with her in a way almost nobody else at court risks being.
characters.name: Kile Woodwork

characters.description: Kile's younger sister, who grew up in the palace and has spent her life behaving as though a crown were owed to her. She is a persistent irritation to Eadlyn and rather less secure than her performance suggests.
characters.name: Josie Woodwork

characters.description: Eadlyn's maid and, though it took Eadlyn a long time to admit it, her friend. She tells the princess uncomfortable truths and keeps her steady while the palace is in crisis.
characters.name: Neena

characters.description: One of the remaining Selected, a young man of Finnish descent whose enthusiasm survives everything and who still speaks almost no English. He cooks, he is entirely sincere, and every word between him and Eadlyn passes through his translator.
characters.name: Henri Jaakoppi

characters.description: Henri's translator, present at every conversation between Henri and the princess and, by virtue of not being a candidate, the one person at the palace with nothing to gain from her. Eadlyn finds his company easier than anyone's, which is an increasingly awkward fact.
characters.name: Erik

characters.description: One of the remaining Selected, good-humored and far more interested in design and tailoring than in politics.
characters.name: Hale Garner

characters.description: One of the remaining Selected, composed and unsentimental, who treats the competition as a negotiation rather than a courtship and is frank with Eadlyn about what an arrangement between them would and would not be.
characters.name: Ean Cabel

characters.description: One of the remaining Selected, warm and openly affectionate, and one of the men Eadlyn came to like before she was prepared to like any of them.
characters.name: Fox

characters.description: The son of August and Georgia Illéa, who led the Northern rebels a generation ago and helped bring down the caste system. Confident, media-friendly, and popular with exactly the people the palace has failed to reach, he offers Eadlyn his family's goodwill and his public support at a moment when she badly needs both.
characters.name: Marid Illéa

recaps.ending: Eadlyn refuses the marriage that would have been most useful to her and makes the choice she actually wants. She exposes what the Illéas were doing, releases the remaining Selected without humiliating any of them, and tells Kile and Henri the truth to their faces rather than through an announcement. Then she goes on live television and tells the country that she has chosen Eikko, Henri's translator: not one of the Selected, not titled, not the political asset her advisers would have picked. In the same period Maxon and America step down, Maxon abdicating so that he can care for his wife and give his daughter the throne outright rather than a regency, and Eadlyn is crowned queen of Illéa. Ahren and Camille return from France, and the breach in the family is closed. America recovers. Eadlyn ends the book as a young queen who has learned to rule by being trusted rather than obeyed, married to a commoner she chose openly, with the monarchy intact and the country's confidence in it restored.
recaps.in_short: With her mother recovering from a heart attack and her father refusing to leave the queen's side, Eadlyn Schreave is made regent and must run Illéa while finishing the Selection she never wanted. Six young men remain, and this time she cannot treat them as scenery. She grows closer to Kile, to the irrepressible Henri, and above all to Erik, Henri's translator, who is not a candidate and therefore not permitted to matter. Marid Illéa, son of the rebel leaders who helped end the caste system, offers her his family's popularity and a public alliance, and Eadlyn takes it before discovering that the Illéas intend to replace the monarchy with themselves at the head of an elected government, and that her courtship is the lever. She exposes them, releases the Selected honestly, and announces on live television that she has chosen Eikko, a commoner with no title at all. Maxon and America abdicate, Eadlyn is crowned queen, and Ahren and Camille come home.

recaps.text: Previously: twenty years after King Maxon abolished Illéa's caste system, the country is in unrest, because money and old prejudice have quietly done the work the castes used to do. Maxon also changed the succession so that his firstborn would inherit regardless of gender, making his daughter Eadlyn the first woman named heir. Cold, controlled, and uninterested in marrying anyone, Eadlyn agreed to hold a Selection of her own purely to distract the country. Thirty-five young men came to the palace, among them Kile Woodwork, who had grown up there and whom she had never liked. She treated the whole thing as theater, staging a kiss for the press and dismissing a candidate who handled her roughly, but the men refused to remain props: she came to like Kile, warmed to the guileless Henri, and found herself looking forward to conversations with Erik, Henri's translator, who was not a candidate at all. Then her twin brother Ahren, tired of being overlooked, eloped to France with Princess Camille, leaving a letter warning Eadlyn that the succession now rested on her alone. The shock brought on their mother's heart attack, and the previous book ended with the queen's survival unknown.

Queen America survives, but she is seriously ill and needs surgery and a long recovery, and Maxon will not leave her. He hands the running of the country to Eadlyn, who becomes regent in everything but name. Six of the Selected remain in the palace while she takes on a workload she has been trained for but never carried alone, in a country still angry about the failures of the post-caste settlement and now unsettled by a prince who left. Ahren writes from France; Eadlyn is not ready to forgive him. The Selection, which she began as a distraction, has become an obligation she cannot postpone, because the throne needs a settled succession and she is now the whole of it.

Ruling makes Eadlyn better at the Selection rather than worse at it. She stops staging and starts asking the remaining men what they would actually do with a position at her side, and finds their answers genuinely useful. Kile talks to her honestly about the life he wants, Henri's cheerfulness is a relief in a grim household, and every conversation with Henri necessarily includes Erik. Neena keeps her upright, her brother Kaden proves steadier than she expected, and Josie is a constant irritation. Eadlyn also begins to see how much of the country's anger is directed at a palace that has not listened, and she starts looking for a way to reach the people her family lost.

Marid Illéa approaches the palace. The son of August and Georgia Illéa, the Northern rebel leaders who helped bring down the castes a generation ago, he is charming, comfortable with the press, and popular with exactly the citizens the crown has failed to reach. He offers Eadlyn his family's goodwill and a public alliance, and the pairing is instantly successful: the coverage is warm, the protests quieten, and Eadlyn is credited with mending a historic rift. She is aware of how useful he is to her and treats the arrangement accordingly. At the same time she is aware that the person she is happiest talking to is Erik, who has no title, no place in the Selection, and no business being considered at all.

Eadlyn narrows the field further, and does it decently. When two of the remaining Selected turn out to be in love with each other, she releases them quietly rather than exposing them, and other men leave for reasons of their own. Her feelings for Erik become impossible to explain away, and she has no framework for them: a queen is expected to marry a candidate, an ally, or an asset, and he is none of these. Her mother's slow recovery, her father's exhaustion, and the constant weight of governing leave her increasingly clear about what she actually values and increasingly aware of how little of it the Selection was designed to deliver.

The Illéas' real intentions surface. Marid's family does not want a marriage into the monarchy; they want the monarchy replaced by an elected government with themselves at the head of it, and Marid's courtship of Eadlyn has been a means of positioning that argument in public. Eadlyn realizes she has been used as a stage prop in her own capital, exactly as she once used the Selection. It is a hard lesson in what she has been doing to other people, and it forces her to decide what the crown is actually for and whether she can defend it on any grounds other than inheritance.

Eadlyn moves against the Illéas' plan and settles the Selection on her own terms. She stops calculating which marriage would be most useful and admits, to herself and then to the people it concerns, that she loves Eikko. She is honest with Kile, who has wanted a life outside the palace all along, and with Henri, whose translator she has fallen for. What she has learned as regent has changed the question she is answering: not who would make the best consort for the throne, but what kind of queen the country would actually trust, and whether she is willing to be that in public.

Eadlyn exposes what the Illéas were attempting, releases the remaining Selected without humiliating any of them, and then goes on live television to tell the country that she has chosen Eikko, Henri's translator, who holds no title and was never a candidate. Maxon and America step down, Maxon abdicating so that he can care for his wife and hand his daughter the throne outright, and Eadlyn is crowned queen of Illéa. Ahren and Camille return from France and the family is whole again; America recovers. Eadlyn marries the man she chose, having learned to rule by earning trust rather than demanding obedience, with the monarchy intact and the country's confidence in it rebuilt.

characters.description: A seventeen-year-old mortal raised in the High Court of Faerie by the man who murdered her parents. Stolen out of the human world as a small child alongside her twin, Taryn, and their half-fey older sister, she has grown up in the household of Madoc, the High King's grand general, with every comfort and no safety: she can be enchanted, she cannot lie, and the fey children she studies beside despise her for being human. Stubborn and combative, she trains with a sword, answers cruelty with defiance rather than retreat, and wants the one thing her adoptive father will not take seriously: a knighthood and a place at court that would make her impossible to dismiss.
characters.name: Jude Duarte

characters.description: Jude's twin sister, raised beside her in Madoc's household. Where Jude answers the court's hostility with defiance, Taryn believes survival lies in giving the fey no reason to notice her at all: she keeps her head down, avoids provoking Cardan's circle, and intends to marry into Faerie and be safe. She urges Jude to stop fighting battles she cannot win, and she has a suitor of her own whose name she refuses to say.
characters.name: Taryn Duarte

characters.description: The eldest of the three sisters and the only one who is half fey, with split-pupilled cat eyes and the ability to enchant mortals. Madoc is her father, which is why he took all three girls when he destroyed the rest of their family. She refuses to accept Faerie or the man who raised her, spends as much time as she can in the human world, and keeps a mortal girlfriend there who does not know what she is.
characters.name: Vivienne

characters.description: A redcap and the High King's grand general: a war-loving fey soldier who killed Jude's mother, once his own wife and long since fled from him, along with the human man she had married, then carried all three of their daughters back to Faerie and raised them as his own because his sense of honour demanded it. He is affectionate, indulgent and entirely unrepentant, teaches Jude swordwork, and treats her ambition to be knighted as a child's passing fancy. He loves battle for its own sake.
characters.name: Madoc

characters.description: Madoc's fey wife, pale-skinned and white-haired, who joined the household after the mortal girls did and has never trusted them. She fears they are a danger to her small son and keeps them at a careful distance while observing every courtesy of family life.
characters.name: Oriana

characters.description: Oriana's young son, a small horned fey boy who adores his older sisters and is indulged by the whole household. He is kept well away from the court and its politics.
characters.name: Oak

characters.description: The youngest son of the High King of Elfhame and the cruellest of the court's young nobles, with a tail he keeps hidden under his clothes and a talent for making an audience of everyone present. Landless, disregarded by his own family and given no duties, he spends his time drinking, staging revels and tormenting whoever is easiest to torment. He reserves a particular and unexplained hatred for Jude.
characters.name: Cardan

characters.description: A princess of the Undersea and daughter of its queen, fostered at the High Court and one of Cardan's closest companions. Beautiful and contemptuous, she considers mortals beneath notice and takes an active part in making the Duarte sisters miserable.
characters.name: Nicasia

characters.description: A young fey lord in Cardan's circle and the most physically dangerous of them. Where the others humiliate the mortal sisters for sport, he escalates, and he does not appear to need an audience.
characters.name: Valerian

characters.description: A fey lord with fox-red hair and amber eyes, one of Cardan's companions but the only one who takes no obvious pleasure in the group's cruelty. Playful and hard to read, he is drawn to drama for its own sake and begins seeking Jude out, offering her the kind of attention no one at court has offered her before.
characters.name: Locke

characters.description: The High King's second son and his chosen heir, poised and outwardly gracious, expected to be crowned at the coming coronation. He keeps a private company of spies and assassins, and he takes an interest in Jude, seeing a use for a mortal willing to bind herself to his service.
characters.name: Prince Dain

characters.description: The ageing High King of Elfhame, who has ruled for centuries and now means to pass the crown to one of his children and step down. Remote and visibly tired of governing, he presides over a court whose quarrels no longer seem to interest him.
characters.name: High King Eldred

characters.description: A pale, quiet fey archer, the marksman of the small band of spies Jude joins. He is the most patient of the three and the one who takes on her training when she needs a steady hand rather than a lesson in cunning.
characters.name: The Ghost

characters.description: An explosives expert with a cloud of white hair, one of the three spies Jude works alongside. Cheerful and practical, she treats a lethal craft as a trade like any other and is generous with what she knows.
characters.name: The Bomb

characters.description: A green-skinned hob and the most experienced of the spies, a thief and lockpick who teaches Jude to open what is locked and to move through the palace unseen. He is blunt about the odds a mortal faces in their line of work.
characters.name: The Roach

characters.description: The High King's eldest son and master of Hollow Hall, a controlling and violent figure who keeps a household of enchanted mortal servants and has custody of his youngest brother, Cardan. Passed over for the throne, he makes little secret of believing himself the better claimant.
characters.name: Prince Balekin

recaps.ending: Jude breaks Madoc's plan by making Cardan an offer he cannot refuse: she will put him on the throne, and in exchange he swears to obey her for a year and a day. Oak, as Prince Dain's son and an heir of the blood, sets the crown on Cardan's head before the court, and Cardan's first commands, every one of them Jude's, undo the coup. Balekin is stripped of his standing and imprisoned in the Tower of Forgetting. Madoc loses his post as grand general and is put out of the palace, outplayed by the mortal daughter he trained and half-admiring of how she did it. Jude sends Oak to the human world to be raised by Vivi and her mortal girlfriend, Heather, keeping the true heir out of every faction's reach until he is old enough to rule without a keeper. Taryn stays in Faerie, engaged to Locke, the breach with her sister unhealed. Cardan sits on the throne of Elfhame as a king nobody expected and nobody trusts, resentful of the leash and unreadable about Jude herself. Jude holds no title anyone would name, only a secret: for a year and a day the High King of Faerie must do as she says, and the clock has already started.
recaps.in_short: Jude Duarte and her twin, Taryn, are mortal girls raised in the High Court of Faerie by Madoc, the fey general who murdered their parents. Despised at court for being human, Jude wants a knighthood and a place no one can take from her; her chief tormentor is Cardan, the High King's youngest son. To gain power of her own she swears herself to Prince Dain, the king's chosen heir, and becomes one of his spies, learning lockpicking, poison tolerance and courtcraft while Cardan's circle escalates from humiliation to attempted murder. Jude kills one of them in self-defence, discovers that the boy courting her has been courting Taryn at the same time, and falls out with her sister. At the coronation the eldest prince, Balekin, murders the High King and most of his heirs, and Madoc is revealed as his ally. Jude gets hold of Cardan, the only remaining heir who can pass the crown, and learns that her small brother Oak is secretly Dain's son and the true heir Madoc intends to rule through. She crowns Cardan instead, on the condition that he obey her for a year and a day, and sends Oak to the human world for safety.

recaps.text: Jude Duarte and her twin, Taryn, are mortals raised in the High Court of Faerie. When they were small, a redcap warrior named Madoc came to their family's house, killed their mother, who had once been his wife and had fled him, killed the human man she had married, and then carried all three of the daughters, including his own half-fey child, Vivienne, back to Elfhame to raise. Ten years on, Jude and Taryn take lessons with the children of the gentry, who despise them for being human. The worst of their tormentors is Cardan, the High King's youngest and least regarded son, with his companions Nicasia, Valerian and Locke. Jude wants a knighthood and a place at court; Madoc, indulgent in everything else, refuses to treat the ambition as real and suggests she would be safer in the mortal world. Taryn wants only to be inoffensive enough to marry into Faerie without incident, and Vivi wants all three of them to leave. At a revel, Cardan's circle forces Jude to eat enchanted fruit, which strips away her self-control and leaves her dancing and weeping for their amusement while the court looks on.

Determined to be something other than a target, Jude goes looking for power. Prince Dain, the High King's chosen heir, offers it: he keeps a private company of spies, and if she swears herself to his service he will knight her once he is crowned. Jude accepts and is bound to him, joining the Court of Shadows, three fey agents known as the Ghost, the Bomb and the Roach, who begin teaching her to pick locks, to fight without honour and to gather what is said at court. To make herself harder to kill and harder to control, she takes small daily doses of faerie poisons to build a tolerance. The realm is preparing for High King Eldred's abdication and Dain's coronation, and Madoc, as grand general, is busy with the arrangements. Locke, alone of Cardan's circle, starts seeking Jude out, and Taryn, who has a suitor of her own she will not name, warns her sister that provoking the gentry will get her killed.

Jude works as Dain's spy, listening at revels and reporting what the gentry say about the succession. Locke's pursuit of her becomes open enough for the court to notice: he brings her to his family's estate, dresses her in finery and enjoys the discomfort her presence causes, and Jude cannot tell whether his interest is genuine or a performance staged for an audience. Cardan's hostility sharpens as Locke's attention grows. Valerian's threats stop being idle; he corners Jude and makes plain that he means her real harm, and she begins carrying a knife and sleeping badly. Taryn, still refusing to name the boy courting her, urges Jude to stop competing with the fey on their own ground, and the distance between the sisters widens.

Valerian breaks into Jude's room at night and tries to kill her. She fights him off and kills him, and the Court of Shadows quietly disposes of the body, leaving Jude shaken and further committed to her double life. At a revel held at Locke's estate she and Cardan are thrown together away from the crowd, and the loathing between them turns briefly into a kiss that appals them both. Working for Dain takes her inside Hollow Hall, the household of Cardan's eldest brother, Balekin, where mortals are kept enchanted and drugged as servants, and where the resentment of a prince passed over for the crown is on open display.

Jude discovers that the suitor Taryn has been hiding is Locke, and that her sister knew all along that he was courting them both. Taryn defends herself: she wants a settled place in Faerie and a husband who can give her one, and she believes Jude's refusal to bend is what endangers them. The quarrel splits the sisters. Jude learns how far Balekin's grievance runs and that he has been gathering allies, and she sees that Cardan lives under his brother's control and violence. The coronation approaches, with Dain expected to take the crown, Madoc arranging the ceremony, and Jude still sworn to a prince whose graciousness she is beginning to distrust.

At the coronation, High King Eldred prepares to pass the crown to Dain before the assembled court, and Balekin springs a coup. His people fall on the royal family: Eldred is killed, several of his children die, and Dain is shot dead by the Ghost, who has been Balekin's man inside the Court of Shadows all along. Madoc is revealed as Balekin's partner in the plot, having chosen the son who will give him the wars he wants.
